Since \(b\not\equiv 0 \pmod{13}\), the bad condition is
\[
b(bc+1)\equiv 0 \pmod{13}
\iff bc+1\equiv 0 \pmod{13}
\iff bc\equiv -1 \pmod{13}.
\]
For each \(b\in\{1,\dots,12\}\), there is exactly one \(c\in\{1,\dots,12\}\) satisfying \(c\equiv -b^{-1}\pmod{13}\). Thus there are \(12\) bad \((b,c)\) pairs.

There are \(12^2=144\) total \((b,c)\) pairs, so valid pairs:
\[
144-12=132.
\]
For each valid pair, \(k\not\equiv0\pmod{13}\), so \(ak\equiv12\pmod{13}\) has exactly one solution \(a\in\{1,\dots,12\}\).

\[
\boxed{132}
\]
